question: What restrictive condition must hold for a yogin of retained semen to count as such rather than by some other means?
premises: A yogin of retained semen is said to become so under a stated condition.
The negation sets apart one class of yogin from another class of yogin.
A truncated instrumental/agentive term marks a contrastive means that is not the operative one here.
inference: The verse draws a class distinction: the title yogin turns on a specific mode of practice, not on a hand-based means, though the exact means remains partially obscured by a lacuna.
uncertainties: Token karata(? is truncated in the transmitted text; its case/derivation cannot be fixed with certainty.
The scope of the contrast between the two yogī tokens is clear in function but not fully explicit due to the lacuna.
plain_english: The yogin with upward-retained semen becomes such — not just any yogin by hand, O beloved.
